page: Amazon Web Services m8idb.96xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose instance utilizing the Nitro hypervisor to deliver massive compute and I/O capacity. The host environment provides 384 dedicated vCPUs distributed across 192 physical Intel cores clocked at 3.9 GHz, supporting two threads per physical core. Memory capacity totals 1536 GB, establishing an even 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, typical of balanced general-purpose infrastructure.

A notable hardware characteristic of the m8idb.96xlarge is its bundled local storage array, offering 22,800 GB of high-speed NVMe SSD capacity. This massive instance store layer facilitates workloads that cannot afford the network round-trips of remote block storage. For network-intensive interactions, the instance provides a 400 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, accommodating massive east-west traffic and high-volume data ingest.

From an efficiency perspective, the m8idb.96xlarge maximizes resource consolidation within a single compute instance, reducing distributed clustering overhead. However, the absence of discrete GPU acceleration restricts its utility for hardware-accelerated machine learning training. Additionally, because instance store volumes are ephemeral, applications must account for data durability through replication or continuous snapshots. The instance is optimally configured for large distributed databases, high-throughput caching systems, batch data processing, and large-scale enterprise microservices.
description: Amazon Web Services m8idb.96xlarge is a general-purpose instance built on the Nitro hypervisor, delivering high compute density and balanced resources. It is powered by dedicated Intel x86_64 processors clocked at 3.9 GHz, comprising 192 physical cores and 384 vCPUs with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The system integrates 1536 GB of system memory, matching the standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio at 4 GB per vCPU. Storage architecture features 22,800 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity, providing substantial on-box storage for applications demanding rapid input/output throughput. Networking performance is established at a 400 Gbps baseline bandwidth without discrete GPU acceleration. The combination of dense vCPU count, large memory array, vast local NVMe capacity, and high-throughput networking makes this instance type cost-effective for large-scale enterprise deployments requiring node consolidation, distributed transactional databases, real-time analytics, and high-bandwidth caching tiers.
